raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with multiple pleural thickenings and marked effusion, along with immunoreactivity for calretinin, AE1/AE3, D2-40, and Wilms tumor protein 1, is consistent with malignant pleural mesothelioma. The disease's stability after treatment and subsequent development of a nodular growth on the tongue, which was found to be a metastasis with similar immunoreactive properties, further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sarcomatoid malignant mesothelioma

rejected.label: Biphasic malignant mesothelioma
rejected.why: While biphasic mesothelioma contains both epithelioid and sarcomatoid components, the described pathology primarily highlights epithelioid features without clear evidence of a significant sarcomatoid component.

rejected.label: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: The immunoreactivity profile, particularly the positivity for calretinin and Wilms tumor protein 1, and the clinical presentation are more consistent with malignant mesothelioma than epithelioid hemangioendothelioma.

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene, along with symptoms such as progressive dysarthria, dysphagia, cognitive impairment, vertical gaze palsy, tongue atrophy, and pyramidal signs, supports this diagnosis. The severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia on 11C-CFT PET imaging also aligns with frontotemporal dementia, particularly given the genetic finding.

rejected.label: Progressive supranuclear palsy
rejected.why: While vertical gaze palsy is a hallmark of progressive supranuclear palsy, the genetic finding of a TBK1 pathogenic variant and the broader range of symptoms better support TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia.

rejected.label: Frontotemporal dementia
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia. The specific genetic finding points more precisely to TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia.

rejected.label: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
rejected.why: Although tongue atrophy and pyramidal signs could suggest amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, the combination of cognitive impairment, vertical gaze palsy, and the specific genetic mutation points away from this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Corticobasal degeneration
rejected.why: This condition often presents with asymmetric parkinsonism and alien limb syndrome, which are not mentioned in the case. The genetic and imaging findings better support TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia.

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute coronary syndrome with recurrent chest pain and electrocardiographic changes
salient_findings: Paroxysmal chest pain occurring 5 times during the day
Elevated cardiac troponin I level
ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR on initial ECG
key_facts: Patient presented to the emergency department with chest pain
Chest pain was paroxysmal and occurred 5 times during the day
Each episode of chest pain lasted 15 to 30 minutes
Blood pressure was 106/52 mm Hg
Pulse rate was 64 beats per minute
Chest auscultation revealed normal breath and heart sounds with no murmurs
Hemogram, serum electrolyte levels, kidney and liver function tests, B-type natriuretic peptide and D-dimer levels were all within normal limits
Cardiac troponin I level was elevated at 25 ng/mL
Initial ECG revealed sinus rhythm, ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, Q wave in lead III, and ST-segment depression in leads I, II, aVL, aVF, and V2 to V6
Repeated ECG showed sinus bradycardia, Q-wave amplitude deepening, ST-segment falling back to equipotential line, and T-wave inversion in lead III
Coronary angiography showed total occlusion of the right coronary artery and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery
